text: Binary GA: A Worked Example Problem: maximize f (x ) = x 2 subject to x ∈ [0, 31]. Key idea ▶ The problem lives in phenotype space (x ). ▶ The GA operates on binary strings (genotype). Takeaway GA does not search the problem space directly. 40 / 48 Representation (Genotype ↔ Phenotype) Encode x ∈ [0, 31] using a 5-bit string b = b4b3b2b1b0 ∈ {0, 1}5 ⇒ x = integer(b). Examples: ▶ 010012 = 9 ▶ 111112 = 31 Takeaway Binary encoding discretizes a numeric decision into a finite search space. 41 / 48 Step 1: Initialize Population and Evaluate Fitness Population size N = 4 (kept tiny so every step is visible). ID Binary string x Fitness f (x ) = x 2 A 01001 9 81 B 10100 20 400 C 00110 6 36 D 11100 28 784 Takeaway Fitness evaluation happens in phenotype space (on x ), not on bits. 42 / 48 Step 2: Parent Selection (Tournament, k = 2) We use tournament selection with k = 2. Example tournaments: ▶ (A vs C) → A ▶ (B vs D) → D ▶ (A vs B) → B ▶ (C vs D) → D Selected parents: [A, D, B, D] Takeaway Selection pressure biases reproduction toward higher fitness, not perfection. 43 / 48 Step 3: One-Point Crossover (pc = 0.8) Pair parents: (A, D) and (B, D). Assume crossover occurs (with probability pc ) and choose cut after bit 3: A : 010|01 D : 111|00 O1 : 01000 O2 : 11101 Second pair (same cut point): B : 101|00 D : 111|00 O3 : 10100 O4 : 11100 Takeaway Crossover recombines existing building blocks into new candidates. 44 / 48 Step 4: Bit-Flip Mutation (pm ≈ 1/L) Each bit flips independently with probability pm ≈ 1 L , L = 5 ⇒ pm = 0.2. Example mutation events: ▶ 01000 → 01010 (one bit flipped) ▶ 11101 → 11101 (no mutation) Offspring population O0 after mutation: Offspring Binary x O1 01010 10 O2 11101 29 O3 10100 20 O4 11100 28 Takeaway Mutation is rare but persistent: it reintroduces lost alleles over time. 45 / 48 Step 5: Replacement and Elitism We apply generational replacement with elitism. ▶ Best individual in P0: D = 11100 (x = 28, f = 784) ▶ Elitism: copy D into P1 ▶ Fill remaining slots with the best offspring from O0 New population P1: {11100, 11101, 10100, 01010} Takeaway Elitism guarantees the current best is not lost (but increases pressure). 46 / 48 What Just Happened? (Interpretation + Diagnostics) Observations: ▶ Best improved: 28 2 → 29 2 ▶ Population drifted toward larger x ▶ Diversity decreased slightly (more high-bit patterns) Diagnostic questions: ▶ If we increase tournament size k, do we converge faster and risk collapse? ▶ If we reduce pm, do we lose alleles permanently? ▶ If we increase elitism, do we freeze the population structure? Takeaway GA behavior emerges from interaction of selection, variation, and representation. 47 / 48
